reasoning: Both are correct, reactive Vide hotbars that clean up BlockTypeChanged and pass all checks. B wins narrowly: it shrinks the bar to fit the screen width while keeping tappable sizes, stops taps in the gaps from passing through to placement, and stays in scope. A adds a larger Screen module with connections that are never disconnected, and its phone fit relies on fixed sizes.

criteria.note: Hud.luau builds the ScreenGui inside the hud component, and Main.client.luau calls Vide.mount(hud, playerGui) once.
BackgroundColor3 and the UIStroke Color/Thickness are functions that call props.IsSelected(), which reads the `selected` source updated by both Select and BlockTypeChanged.
Hud calls cleanup(BlockPlacer.BlockTypeChanged:Connect(...)), but Screen.luau leaves its camera and PreferredInput connections open at module level forever.
The hotbar loops over props.BlockTypes and calls slot({BlockType, Index, IsSelected, Select, Metrics, ...}).
localPlayer:WaitForChild("PlayerGui") runs in Main before Vide.mount.
The COMPACT metrics give 64 px slots and a bar about 356 px wide plus CoreUISafeInsets, which likely clears the touch controls, but the size isn't tied to the screen width.
Strictly typed and passes all checks; adds a broader Screen module, and the bar frame lacks Active, so taps in the gaps may place blocks.
The Hotbar component creates everything inside the function passed to Vide.mount in Main.client.luau.
BackgroundColor3 and the stroke Color/Thickness are functions that call isSelected(), which reads the `selected` source updated by select() and BlockTypeChanged.
Both the BlockTypeChanged and KeyboardEnabled connections are wrapped in cleanup().
It loops over BlockTypes.List and calls Slot({blockType, index, selected, select, showKeyHints}).
WaitForChild("PlayerGui") is evaluated as an argument before mount runs.

The UIScale is clamped so the bar takes at most 50% of the screen width with a 0.7 floor (slots about 45 px or more), with CoreUISafeInsets, which keeps it centred between the thumbstick and jump button.
Focused single file that passes all checks; Active=true on the bar stops taps from passing through; no --!strict.

strengths: Clean split into Hotbar/Hud components with a props-driven slot
Bindings are reactive throughout, including derived metrics
cleanup on BlockTypeChanged; updates the highlight immediately on tap
weaknesses: The Screen module adds scope and keeps connections open at module level
No Active on the bar, so taps between slots may reach the world
Phone fit relies on fixed compact sizes rather than the screen width

strengths: Explicit width-based scaling that guarantees phone fit and tap size
Active bar keeps taps in the gaps from passing through to placement
Compact, focused change with a selected-name label
weaknesses: Sets some properties Vide already defaults
Slot takes the selected source rather than an isSelected binding
